BEHIND THE ATMOSPHERE

A little science.
A different perspective.

The landscape is real elevation data, rendered in 3D by MapLibre. The weather is an interactive simulation.

01 / Volume, not a backdrop

Each viewing ray travels through a three-dimensional noise field. Cloud density accumulates into soft, sunlit volumes anchored in meters above sea level.

02 / Mountains come first

The terrain depth buffer stops each ray at the mountain surface. Peaks can rise through the clouds; nearby clouds can veil distant slopes.

03 / Follow the wind

Clouds move automatically whenever wind speed is above zero. Wind direction means where the wind comes from: a westerly wind (270°) carries clouds east. Motion is shown at six times real time so you can see the drift. Set 0 km/h for still clouds, or use Pause clouds.

04 / Explore the mountains

Choose a famous summit to move the camera, or zoom out for a wider view. City names show selected cities and gateway towns in the Alps and Himalaya, with more detail as you zoom in. The volumetric cloud view is intended for regional exploration.

Terrain: Mapterhorn. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics and the GIS User Community. Built with MapLibre GL JS and WebGL 2. Requires internet access for map tiles.
